Thus, to ensure Olympic athletes are judged fairly,
we should start incorporating artificial intelligence (AI)
into the process used to evaluate athletes’ performances.
So how do artificially intelligent judges work?
First, an AI model is trained on countless hours of
footage, effectively teaching it to identify tricks,
distinguish between a good landing and an okay landing,
and see small flaws, such as the slight under rotation
of a spin. Then, during a competition, a handful of
high-definition cameras record an athlete and construct
a three-dimensional image of their body. [
B
] The image
is then fed into the trained AI model, which precisely
analyzes each angle and movement beyond the
capabilities of a human.
Some might argue that AI will soon replace human
judges altogether, but this is not the case. Elements like
artistry
and
style
(what make these subjective sports so
special) are nearly impossible for AI to evaluate, thus,
it’s vital that we keep humans at the center of judging
these sports. [
C
] However, even at their best, humans
can miss things or grow fatigued at the end of a long day.
